text: About 13.5 hectares (3.9% of the 345.6-hectare property) of native forest was lost in 2025, based on satellite data. The area affected was confirmed as native forest by Uruguay’s official 2021 forest map. However, this loss is not yet fully corroborated—it’s the latest observation (2025), so we can’t yet tell if it’s permanent or if the land has regrown. The cause (e.g., logging, fire, or natural disturbance) also isn’t clear from the data. While the evidence strongly suggests forest loss occurred, further monitoring would be needed to confirm long-term impacts or legality.
